title: Distributional Network of Networks for Modeling Data Heterogeneity

problem.claim: Data heterogeneity across domains creates a need for methods that model domain adaptation and out-of-distribution generalization.

gap.claim: Existing methods generally do not explicitly explain adaptive propagation of label information from source domains to the target domain, and their neural-network convergence has received little theoretical study.

contributions.claim: TENON is a generic distributional network-of-networks framework in which nodes represent domains with domain-specific networks, main-network edges represent domain similarity, and within-network edges represent sample similarity.
TENON unifies within-domain label smoothness and cross-domain parameter smoothness.
The framework yields TENON-DA and TENON-OOD for domain adaptation and out-of-distribution generalization, formulated respectively as transductive and inductive distribution learning problems.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The analysis covers TENON's convergence and optimality.
The effectiveness and efficiency of TENON-DA and TENON-OOD are reported as verified theoretically and empirically.

narrative_sequence.summary: Data heterogeneity is widespread, motivating domain adaptation and out-of-distribution generalization.
Existing algorithms do not explicitly explain adaptive label propagation across domains, and neural-network convergence is insufficiently understood theoretically.
TENON models domains and samples as a network of networks and unifies within-domain label smoothness with cross-domain parameter smoothness.
The authors analyze TENON's convergence and optimality and connect its formulations to transductive and inductive distribution learning.
TENON-DA and TENON-OOD are developed, with effectiveness and efficiency reported as verified theoretically and empirically.
